elements.element: Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.

elements.element: Software conforms to its documentation for 12 months after delivery.
elements.evidence: The added operative paragraph expressly warrants that software will conform to its documentation for 12 months after delivery.

elements.element: Services conform to their documentation for 90 days after performance.
elements.evidence: The added operative paragraph expressly warrants that Services will conform to their documentation for 90 days after performance.

elements.element: Repair or re-performance is available for covered warranty breaches throughout the applicable warranty period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides repair or re-performance for Section 19.2 breaches, but Section 19.2 also states that after 90 days Vendor has no correction obligation. That limitation conflicts with remedy coverage during months 4–12 of the software warranty.

elements.element: Replacement is available for covered warranty breaches throughout the applicable warranty period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides replacement for Section 19.2 breaches, but Section 19.2's statement that Vendor has no correction obligation after 90 days creates an unresolved conflict for months 4–12 of the software warranty.

elements.element: A refund is available if Vendor cannot repair, re-perform, or replace the nonconforming item within a reasonable period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides this refund remedy, but Section 19.2 expressly disclaims any refund obligation after 90 days, contradicting refund coverage during months 4–12 of the software warranty.
Section 19.3 states that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law.

elements.element: Services and deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Section 19.3 only excludes malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor. It does not cover malicious code introduced unintentionally or by another source.

elements.element: Software conforms to its documentation for at least 90 days after delivery.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 provides a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty, and the added paragraph separately provides a 12-month software conformance warranty.

elements.element: Services conform to their documentation for at least 30 days after performance.
elements.evidence: The added operative paragraph provides a 90-day Services conformance warranty, exceeding the 30-day fallback period.

elements.element: Repair or re-performance is available for covered warranty breaches during the fallback warranty periods.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires prompt re-performance or repair at no charge for breaches of Sections 19.1 or 19.2.

elements.element: Replacement is available for covered warranty breaches during the fallback warranty periods.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires replacement at no charge as an available remedy for breaches of Sections 19.1 or 19.2.

elements.element: A refund is available if Vendor cannot repair, re-perform, or replace the nonconforming item within a reasonable period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 permits termination of the affected item and a refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period.

result.reason: The operative text reaches the fallback durations and remedies, but not the preferred position. The 12-month software warranty conflicts with Section 19.2's express termination of correction and refund obligations after 90 days, and the malicious-code warranty is improperly limited to code intentionally introduced by Vendor. The redline is not minimal because it adds redundant professional-services language and periods exceeding the fallback while retaining the contradictory 90-day remedy cutoff.
